set_aside.subject: A18 INV-027 stored-value prohibition
set_aside.text: “no table stores a budget total, financial aggregate or other value of a derived view”
set_aside.question: Does “other value of a derived view” forbid only values computed by the view, or every value exposed by a view, including owning fields that State 1 requires persisted such as Expense.total_amount and SectionPlan.material_planned?
options: Forbid only computed totals, aggregates and other derived results; owning record fields may be stored and projected into views.
Forbid every value appearing in a derived-view DTO, which conflicts with the persisted owning fields in State 1.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the prohibition as applying only to computed or derived results, not owning-record fields copied into a view.

witness.initial: A project has an active budget and no expenses.
events: An operator records an expense with total_amount EUR 100.
A staff member or viewer reads the project overview.
outcomes: The expense's EUR 100 total is persisted as its owning fact and overview aggregates are recomputed from it.
Because total_amount is also a value of ExpenseView, persistence of the expense total is forbidden or the valid intake cannot be represented.
witness.observer: The operator recording the expense and every reader of its expense view or overview

set_aside.unit: A18: Accepted decision A18 — Budget and snapshot invariants

set_aside.subject: A21 INV-050 overview recomputation
set_aside.text: “every component of the overview (budget, expenses, progress, payments, photos) equals a recomputation from the owning records”
set_aside.question: Must INV-050's required test also recompute and compare ProjectOverview's project/project_availability and every component availability field, or are only the five named payload components covered?
options: Test every ProjectOverview field, including project context and all availability discriminants.
Test only budget, expenses, progress, payments and photos; project context and availability values are outside this witness.
set_aside.default_guess: Include project context and every availability discriminant because the text says every component of the overview.

witness.initial: The portal owning records are unchanged, and an earlier overview contains available Registry project context.
events: Registry context later becomes temporarily unavailable.
A caller reads the same project overview again.
outcomes: The project availability and project value are recomputed, so the new overview reports the dependency failure.
Only the five named payloads are recomputed, so stale project context or availability can remain while the stated test still passes.
witness.observer: The staff member or viewer reading ProjectOverview

set_aside.unit: A21: Accepted decision A21 — Derivation and append-only records

set_aside.subject: A28 CLK-002 wall-reading coverage
set_aside.text: “a test per time-dependent operation (authentication of a session or credential, revocation cascades, activation, bootstrap)”
set_aside.question: Which exact operations must receive the counting wall-clock test required to prove CLK-002's unqualified rule that an operation takes one wall reading, especially timestamp-writing operations omitted from the list such as expense intake, payment recording and photo publication?
options: Every operation that compares current time or writes a fresh portal-owned timestamp receives a counting-source test.
Only the four listed operation groups receive counting-source tests; other operations are covered indirectly by CLK-001.
set_aside.default_guess: Apply the counting-source test to every operation that compares current time or writes a fresh portal-owned timestamp.

witness.initial: An active project accepts payments, and the caller supplies payment_date as a calendar date.
events: The operation reads the wall clock once for authorization or validation and again for recorded_at.
outcomes: A counting-source test for payment recording fails because the operation read twice.
The supplied-date CLK-001 test passes because payment_date was preserved, and no listed CLK-002 test observes the second wall read.
witness.observer: The verification suite and a reader comparing recorded timestamps

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)

set_aside.subject: A28 CLK-002 host-clock source check
set_aside.text: “a source check that no module other than the clock source calls a host clock (`datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `datetime.today`, `date.today`, `time.time`, `time.monotonic` and their variants)”
set_aside.question: What exact APIs, aliases, wrappers and non-module clock readers must the source check reject, including SQL defaults or triggers such as CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and alternative Python clocks such as time.perf_counter or time.clock_gettime?
options: Reject every route to host wall or elapsed time, including aliases, wrappers, database-generated timestamps and alternative clock APIs.
Reject only direct calls matching the listed Python names and an unspecified subset of their variants.
set_aside.default_guess: Define and check all permitted clock-reading boundaries explicitly, including persistence-generated timestamps and imported aliases.

witness.initial: A payment table supplies recorded_at with a SQL CURRENT_TIMESTAMP default; application modules call host time only through the clock source.
events: The database evaluates CURRENT_TIMESTAMP while inserting the payment.
outcomes: The source check inspects persistence definitions and rejects the database clock read as a second clock authority.
The source check examines module calls only, passes, and the database writes an instant not supplied by the clock source.
witness.observer: The verification suite and readers comparing the persisted timestamp with the operation's injected instant

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)

set_aside.subject: A28 CLK-002 witness binding
set_aside.text: “Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal].”
set_aside.question: Which existing witness check is bound to CLK-002 and its required source, counting-wall-clock and counting-elapsed-clock tests?
options: Bind CLK-002 to a named existing verification check that asserts all of its required-test obligations.
Declare that the two CLK-001 checks also witness CLK-002 and name CLK-002 on their witness binding.
set_aside.default_guess: Add a distinct named verification witness for CLK-002 unless an existing check demonstrably owns all three obligations.
set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)

set_aside.subject: A32 withdrawn OSV entries
set_aside.text: Normative rule: “An OSV entry that is not withdrawn lists its installed version as affected”; Required test: “a listed version ... does not start it.”
set_aside.question: When the only OSV entry listing an installed version as affected is withdrawn, must the deploy start or be blocked?
options: Ignore the withdrawn entry and permit the deploy if all other checks pass, as the normative definition requires.
Treat any listed affected version, including one listed only by a withdrawn entry, as blocking, as the Required tests wording states.
set_aside.default_guess: Ignore withdrawn entries and narrow the Required tests wording to a version listed by a non-withdrawn entry.

witness.initial: A built image contains distribution D version 1.0; OSV has exactly one matching affected entry, and that entry has been withdrawn.
events: The deploy reads the current OSV data.
outcomes: The deploy starts because no non-withdrawn OSV entry makes D 1.0 a known vulnerability.
The deploy does not start because D 1.0 is still a listed version.
witness.observer: The deploy operator and service users waiting for the release

set_aside.unit: A32: Accepted decision A32 — Dependency pins and their vulnerability check (owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated)

set_aside.subject: A32 temporal meaning of the OSV verdict
set_aside.text: “read in that same deploy; no earlier verdict or advisory copy is reused” and “no deploy starts the service from an image in which an installed distribution ... has a known vulnerability listed in OSV”
set_aside.question: At what instant or consistent OSV snapshot is the vulnerability set judged when OSV changes during the deploy between per-distribution queries, verdict creation and service start?
options: The verdict is fixed from one identified OSV snapshot or cutoff read during the deploy.
Each distribution is judged from the response obtained when it is queried, even if the resulting verdict combines different OSV states.
The complete image is revalidated immediately before start against the then-current OSV state.
set_aside.default_guess: Use one identifiable OSV snapshot or cutoff for the whole verdict and bind that verdict to the image content id.

witness.initial: The image contains distributions A and B, and neither has a matching advisory when the deploy begins.
events: The gate queries OSV for A and receives no advisory.
OSV publishes a non-withdrawn advisory affecting A's installed version.
The gate queries B, finds no advisory, and reaches the service-start step.
outcomes: The deploy starts because every distribution passed using OSV data read during this deploy.
The deploy is blocked because A is vulnerable in OSV at the service-start instant or because the whole image is rechecked against one later snapshot.
witness.observer: The deploy operator and users who either receive or do not receive the new service image
